questions.q: In the worked example, compressing a 14-turn, 6,400-token conversation into a rolling summary plus the last 3 turns verbatim produced roughly what result?
options: A slightly larger transcript than the original
Exactly the same token count, just reformatted
1,850 tokens — about 71% smaller, with the key facts still carried forward
A transcript with all turns removed entirely
questions.explain: The worked example shows rolling summarization shrinking the conversation from 6,400 to 1,850 tokens while preserving the facts needed going forward.

questions.q: What is the key risk of truncation compared to rolling summarization?
options: Anything only mentioned in a dropped turn is genuinely gone, not just compressed into a summary
Truncation always costs more tokens than summarization
Truncation requires an extra model call to run
Truncation cannot be used on conversation history, only on documents
questions.explain: Truncation drops turns outright with no summary, so information unique to those turns is lost entirely, unlike summarization which retains a compact version of it.

questions.q: In the structured extraction example, what did the three-field JSON object capture from the policy excerpt?
options: The entire original paragraph, reformatted as JSON
A summary of every policy in the company
Only the final-sale exclusion rule
refund_days, premium_refund_days, and final_sale_excluded — the decision-relevant facts, not the surrounding prose
questions.explain: Structured extraction pulled exactly the facts a task needs (three fields) out of a longer prose excerpt, dropping the surrounding wording.

questions.q: What does prompt caching address that the other three techniques don't?
options: It summarizes conversation history automatically
It avoids re-processing an unchanged context prefix (like a static system prompt) on every call, rather than shrinking what's included
It deletes old tool schemas permanently
It extracts structured facts from documents
questions.explain: Prompt caching reuses an unchanged prefix instead of resending and reprocessing it — a cost optimization distinct from summarizing, truncating, or extracting content.

questions.q: According to the lesson, how should you decide which compression technique to use?
options: Always use the most aggressive technique available, regardless of task
Never compress context under any circumstances
Pick the lightest technique that still protects the facts your eval set actually checks for
Use a different random technique on every call for variety
questions.explain: The lesson frames the choice as a tradeoff: pick the lightest technique that still preserves what the task actually needs, since every technique risks losing some detail.
